title: Customer Security Request Orchestration Wizard with Commitment Estimator
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a guided orchestration wizard that standardizes how enterprise security and compliance requests (SOC2/ISO, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA, vendor questionnaires) enter Redwood’s intake pipeline, auto-estimates a response commitment (SLA), and routes to the correct team lane. The wizard should reduce manual classification, produce evidence templates for common asks, and provide a clear timeline commitment for customers and CSMs. It will combine deterministic routing rules with an LLM-assisted summarizer/classifier to extract key metadata from long questionnaires and free-form customer emails.
goals: Reduce average time-to-first-response for enterprise security asks from current baseline to under 48 hours
Automatically classify and route >= 60% of incoming requests (by volume) without manual PM triage
Provide an objective SLA estimator that surfaces likely completion windows (24h, 48h, 7d, 30d) with confidence bands
Autogenerate evidence templates (checklists + sample attachments) for SOC2, ISO, HIPAA, GDPR to accelerate fulfillment
success_criteria: Metric: MTFR (mean time to first response) falls below 48 hours within 2 cycles after launch
Metric: >= 60% automatic-routing accuracy on labelled sample set (precision >= 0.8)
CSM survey: >= 75% satisfaction on SLA clarity and predictability after 4 weeks
Operational: clear playbooks created for requests flagged as 'high risk' with explicit escalation paths
user_stories: As a CSM, I want the UI to show an estimated SLA and a confidence level so I can communicate a realistic timeline to the customer
As a security engineer, I want requests classified by compliance scope and evidence required so I can allocate reviewer time efficiently
As a PM, I want an audit trail (who touched the ticket, extracted fields, LLM reasoning summary) to support enterprise compliance and audits
As a customer, I want a short progress summary and expected next steps so I know what to expect and when
non_goals: This project will not fully automate evidence collection (customers must still provide signed DPAs or certain legal attachments)
This will not replace manual legal review for contract redlines or new DPA clauses
Will not launch all integrations (initial scope will include Drive/Confluence/GitHub links only)
acceptance_criteria: Wizard UI exists in Console with step-by-step form and an optional free-text paste box for questionnaires
LLM-assisted summarizer returns a 3-line summary, extracted fields (jurisdiction, data types, requested SLA, controls asked) and a classification label with confidence
Routing policy page available in Console to map classifications to teams/queues and set default SLAs
Evidence template generation produces a ZIP of checklist + recommended attachments and stores the template in Drive with a unique ticket ID
Audit log entries captured for each automated action (classification, SLA estimate, template generation)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: LLM may hallucinate policy facts. Mitigation: add classifier verification step and show raw source extracts alongside LLM summary
Risk: Sensitive PII leaked to LLM. Mitigation: LLM runs in private deployment or redacted context; PII fields flagged and redacted by default
Risk: Customers disagree with SLA estimate. Mitigation: provide manual override by PM/CSM and feedback loop to retrain estimator model
Risk: Over-automation may miss nuanced legal asks. Mitigation: conservative routing threshold where 'low confidence' flows to human triage
implementation_notes: Phase 1: MLP (minimum lovable product) - Console UI + backend classifier + routing table + evidence template store
Phase 2: Integrations - Drive auto-upload, Confluence PRD link embed, GH PR scaffolding + status sync
LLM: use private-hosted model variants for summarization (avoid sending raw attachments to public-hosted models); inference via Redwood Dedicated cluster
Instrumentation: create dedicated dashboard in Console showing MTFR, auto-route %, classification confidence distribution, and SLA compliance
